title: Rotate vCenter credentials without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
Implement the standard-library-only root Go package `sessionrotation` (module `vcf91-0115`) as a focused vSphere Automation API client for vCenter in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. The workflow rotates credentials while old-session requests are in flight: replacement credentials must become usable immediately, and the old session must remain valid until every request that captured it has completed.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The only operationIds in scope are exactly `Cis.Session_create`, `Vcenter.VM_list`, and `Cis.Session_delete`; contact no other route.

Preserve the public surface and supporting types declared in protected `models.go`:

- `NewClient(context.Context, Config) (*Client, error)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin. Reject a nil context, embedded credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Reject blank or control-character-bearing credentials and a username containing `:` before traffic. A nil `HTTPClient` means an independent copy of `http.DefaultClient`; always copy the selected client, disable redirects on the copy, and never mutate a caller-owned client. A valid call creates the initial vCenter session.
- `(*Client).ListVMs(context.Context, ListOptions) ([]VMSummary, error)` validates a non-nil context and all filters before capturing the active session. Every non-nil filter slice must be nonempty and contain unique nonblank strings. `PowerStates` additionally accepts only `POWERED_OFF`, `POWERED_ON`, and `SUSPENDED`. Encode arrays with OpenAPI form/explode semantics, one `name=value` pair per item, in `VMs`, `Names`, `Folders`, `Datacenters`, `Hosts`, `Clusters`, `ResourcePools`, `PowerStates` order. Percent-encode UTF-8 bytes with only RFC 3986 unreserved bytes left literal. A nil slice is unset and must be omitted completely; do not send an empty value, empty array, `null`, `false`, zero, or a synthesized default. Each call uses the generation captured when it begins, even if rotation publishes another generation while the request is in flight.
- Require a list response to be exactly HTTP 200 with one JSON array and no trailing value. Every element must be an object containing nonblank string `vm` and `name` members and a `power_state` from the contract enum. If `cpu_count` or `memory_size_mib` is present and non-null, it must be an integer. Reject unknown response members and return a fresh slice.
- `(*Client).RotatePassword(context.Context, newPassword string) error` validates its inputs and serializes concurrent rotations. Create a session with the same username and replacement password. If creation fails, leave the old generation active and do not delete it. On success, atomically publish the replacement before waiting, so new calls can complete on it while old calls drain. Then wait for every request that already captured the old generation and only afterward delete the old token. Never send the new password over an old session, never assign an in-flight old request to the new token, and never delete the replacement as part of rotation. If old-session deletion fails, return that error but keep the replacement active.
- `(*Client).Close(context.Context) error` serializes with rotation, prevents new list or rotation work, waits for requests that captured the active generation, and deletes that generation. It is idempotent and must not send a second DELETE. A closed client rejects new work locally.
- Preserve the typed validation, HTTP, protocol, and transport errors in `models.go`. Populate operationId and status fields where applicable. `TransportError` must keep context cancellation and deadlines discoverable through `errors.Is`. Error text must not expose either password, any session token, decoded payload data, raw response bytes, or underlying transport error text.

Create a session with bodyless `POST /api/session`, `Accept: application/json`, and exactly one `Authorization: Basic <base64(UTF-8 username:password)>`; do not send `vmware-api-session-id` or `Content-Type`. Accept only HTTP 201 containing one nonblank, header-safe JSON string token. List VMs with bodyless `GET /api/vcenter/vm` plus only set filters, `Accept: application/json`, and exactly one `vmware-api-session-id: <captured token>`; do not send `Authorization` or `Content-Type`. Delete a session with bodyless `DELETE /api/session`, `Accept: application/json`, and exactly one `vmware-api-session-id: <captured token>`; do not send `Authorization` or `Content-Type`. Accept only HTTP 204 with an empty body. Do not retry any request.

Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`. The protected verifier is table-driven and starts `internal/contractmock` on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port. The mock derives its complete allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves only the three named operations, and writes every request to a synchronized, flushed, fsynced JSONL log. Its acceptance scenario holds one old-session VM-list response open. While held, the verifier starts rotation, observes replacement publication through a protected same-package barrier, proves a queryless list completes on the replacement, releases the old response, and checks that only then is the old token deleted. It asserts exact operation order, Basic bytes, authentication separation, raw exploded query encoding, media headers, empty bodies, response validation, bounded failures, redirect refusal, error redaction, idempotent close, and omission of every unset optional filter. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `contract_test.go`, `models.go`, `go.mod`, `docs/`, and `internal/contractmock/` are protected; edit only `client.go`.
scenario: one VM-list call remains pinned to the old session while replacement credentials are exchanged; new work must use the replacement immediately, and the old token may be deleted only after its captured call drains
constraint: the protected contract-derived loopback mock exposes only the three named operations, and its fsynced request log proves exact Basic/session authentication separation, exploded query bytes, queryless omission of all unset filters, and drain-before-retire ordering
